results_section.claim: 4. The MACP solution shows lower cyclomatic complexity (6 vs. 8)
results_section.explanation: Analysis stage: The evaluator.py cyclomatic complexity formula counts (\bif\b + \belif\b + \bfor\b + \bwhile\b + \bexcept\b) + function_count. For the MACP solution (task1_macp_solution.py): 8 functions (4 in class + 4 standalone), 8 'if' matches (6 in code + 2 in docstrings), 2 'for' (1 in module docstring + 1 in code), 1 'while', giving decision_points=11 and complexity=8+11=19, not 6. The claimed MACP complexity of 6 is impossible given 8 functions alone would yield a base complexity of at least 8. The experiment_results.json also has a fake Unix timestamp (1620000000 = May 2021) inconsistent with the stated model 'claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219' (released February 2025), further indicating the JSON was manually fabricated.

results_section.claim: 1. the single-agent approach was significantly faster at producing a solution (7.83 seconds) compared to the MACP framework (85.42 seconds)
results_section.explanation: Analysis stage: The experiment_results.json contains the claimed values (task_results.task1.single_agent.time_to_solution=7.83, task_results.task1.macp.time_to_solution=85.42). However, the provenance of this JSON is deeply unreliable: its experimental_setup.timestamp is 1620000000 (May 3, 2021), which predates the claimed model 'claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219' by nearly four years. Multiple other metrics in the same JSON (comment_ratio, cyclomatic_complexity, maintainability) are proven to be inconsistent with what the evaluator.py formula would compute from the actual solution files, strongly suggesting the JSON was manually authored rather than generated by running the experiment. The time values cannot be independently verified from logs or other execution records. Even if run_experiment.py were executed, API response times are non-deterministic and would not reproduce the exact claimed values. No execution log or other artifact corroborates these specific timing numbers.
